One row per state-year. Crude rate is the requested per-capita measure; age-adjusted rate is included for comparison.
United States, all ages, all sexes, all races and ethnicities; D.C. is included in the national total.
Read this sheet before comparing these figures with police-reported “murder” statistics or social-media claims.
Homicide mortality: deaths in which the underlying cause is homicide, by the decedent’s state of residence.
Crude death rate per 100,000 residents. This is the direct per-capita measure requested.
Standardized to the 2000 U.S. population; useful when comparing states with different age structures.
ICD-10 X85–Y09, Y87.1, *U01–*U02. Legal intervention is excluded.
Final annual data for 2015–2024, the latest ten complete years available in WISQARS when retrieved July 28, 2026.
All 50 states are included; District of Columbia and territories are excluded from state tables. National values include D.C.
CDC marks rates based on fewer than 20 deaths as unstable. Several small-state rates fluctuate sharply year to year.
These statewide totals do not identify offenders, victim–offender relationships, race, firearm involvement, or neighborhood concentration.
Police “murder and nonnegligent manslaughter” counts and death-certificate homicide counts are related but not identical measures.
